proposals.before: Jianwu 2 saw the great altars of soil and grain east of Luoyang, south of the temples—open-air square mounds with a gate.
proposals.after: In Jianwu 2 the grand altars of soil and grain were founded at Luoyang, to the right of the ancestral temples—open-air square mounds with only a walled gateway.
proposals.reason: Chinese 在宗庙之右 means to the right of the ancestral temples; the idiomatic rendering invents “east of Luoyang, south of the temples.”

proposals.before: In the eighth year after the founding of Han someone said that when Zhou rose it founded sacrifice to Hou Ji in the capital; therefore Gaozu ordered She altars named Lingxing established empire-wide.
proposals.after: In the eighth year after the founding of Han someone said that when Zhou rose it founded sacrifice to Hou Ji in the capital; therefore Emperor Gao ordered Lingxing shrines established empire-wide.
proposals.reason: Chinese 立灵星祠 is establishing Lingxing shrines, not She altars renamed Lingxing.

proposals.before: Lingdi, the Jiedu marquis and Hejian prince’s great-great-grandson, likewise raised his ancestors.
proposals.after: Lingdi, the Jiedu marquis and Hejian prince’s great-grandson, likewise raised his ancestors.
proposals.reason: Classical 曾孙 denotes a great-grandson (son’s son’s son); “great-great-grandson” overstates the generation distance.

proposals.before: Emperor Ling, the marquis of Jiedu, a great-great-grandson of the Filial King of Hejian, succeeded and likewise posthumously honored his forebears.
proposals.after: Emperor Ling, the marquis of Jiedu, a great-grandson of the Filial King of Hejian, succeeded and likewise posthumously honored his forebears.
proposals.reason: Same generation error as in the idiomatic line: 曾孙 is great-grandson.

decisions.reason: Chinese 立太社稷于雒阳，在宗庙之右 places the altars at Luoyang to the right of the ancestral temples; the original invents “east of Luoyang, south of the temples,” and 有墙门而已 supports “only a walled gateway.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 立太社稷于雒阳，在宗庙之右，方坛，无屋，有墙门而已

decisions.reason: Chinese 令天下立灵星祠 orders Lingxing shrines established empire-wide; the original’s “She altars named Lingxing” is invented, and 高帝 is correctly rendered Emperor Gao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 于是高帝令天下立灵星祠

decisions.reason: Chinese 河间孝王曾孙 uses 曾孙, the standard term for great-grandson; “great-great-grandson” overstates the generation distance.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 灵帝以河间孝王曾孙解犊侯即位

decisions.reason: Same source term 曾孙 requires great-grandson in the literal line; the proposed replacement matches the Chinese kinship term.
